messages:
jordan: Hey team — just escalated from Acme Payments. After we rotated their API key last night in eu-west, they started seeing intermittent 401s from some of their backend hosts. They say it affects ~10% of requests and clears up after a retry. Customer provided couple of logs and their repro steps. Filing here to coordinate: 

jordan: Repro steps they gave:
1) hit /v1/generate with old key -> 401 (expected)
2) swap to new key in Vault -> 200 for some requests
3) same host will flip back to 401 intermittently for a minute or two

jordan: Example logs from their edge: 
```
2026-03-14T22:03:12Z INFO request id=abc123 status=200 key_fingerprint=sha256:OLD
2026-03-14T22:03:14Z WARN request id=abc124 status=401 reason=invalid_api_key key_fingerprint=sha256:NEW
2026-03-14T22:03:15Z INFO request id=abc125 status=200 key_fingerprint=sha256:NEW
```

jordan: They claim Vault write returned OK at 22:02:50 and we rotated via the scheduled job. No config changes on their side except swapping env var.

maya: looking. tagging @eli on infra side — could be cache at the edge or kube pod env var refresh timing. Did they use sidecar vs env var file reload?

eli: pinging logs. quick Q: did they use the vault agent sidecar (ssorotate) or set env var from secrets store? if sidecar, a stale in-memory cache could be the culprit.

jordan: They say they used the secrets-injector that writes to a file and then SIGHUPs the app (we have their commands). Not sidecar.

tony: hmm, file write + SIGHUP should be atomic. Another possibility: we rotated key in control plane but our regional edge cache (auth cache) still had old fingerprint mapping for a TTL. We have a per-region auth cache with 30s TTL but there was a backlog during deploy.

maya: can we confirm evictions around 22:02:50 in eu-west auth cache? @deploy-bot can you surface cache events?

deploy-bot: Querying auth-cache logs for region=eu-west between 2026-03-14T22:02:40Z and 2026-03-14T22:03:30Z...

deploy-bot: Results: 3 auth-cache misses, 2 scheduled evictions, 1 delayed eviction due to GC pause on node-7 for ~45s.

eli: GC pause on node-7 lines up with backlog. If eviction delayed, some requests would still consult old mapping until eviction runs. That matches intermittent 401s as some requests hit a different node.

jordan: Customer also sent curl from a single host showing flip-flop on same host: 
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer NEW_KEY" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
...
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
...
```

maya: OK. action plan:
- eli: confirm node-7 GC was root cause and check if we saw similar GC pauses recently.
- tony: add a short-term rollout to reduce auth-cache TTL to 10s for eu-west for 1 hour and force eviction.
- jordan: ask customer to restart one of affected hosts as a temp mitigation (their next deploy will do it anyway).

eli: running postmortem queries now. Also checking whether Vault's rewrap / reencrypt process introduced a different fingerprint format (unlikely but check).

tony: I'll schedule TTL change and trigger coordinated eviction. Doing now: `curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/regions/eu-west/cache/evict -d '{"target":"auth"}'` — waiting for confirmation.

ops-bot: Auth cache TTL set to 10s for region eu-west (applied to service auth-cache-v2). Eviction job queued.

ops-bot: Eviction job completed. 5,232 keys evicted from auth-cache across 3 nodes.

eli: GC logs show a 47s STW pause on node-7 at 22:02:52 due to large heap compaction in the authorization agent. That explains delayed eviction. No other anomalies.

maya: Nice catch. jordan, pls relay to customer: we found auth-cache eviction delayed during rotation because of a GC pause on one node which caused stale mappings to persist for ~45s. Short-term: we forced eviction and reduced TTL. Recommend they restart one host (or wait 1 minute) if they still see issues. Long-term: we'll harden by tuning GC on auth agent or using instant invalidation webhook for rotations.

jordan: I'll send that to them. Customer replied: "Appreciate the fast turnaround — we did a quick restart and errors disappeared." They also asked what caused GC pause. I'll iterate and keep thread updated.

tony: follow-up: I'll open a ticket to add an immediate invalidation signal from rotation flow to auth-cache so we don't rely on TTL during rotations.

eli: also adding a health check to alert on STW pauses > 20s for auth nodes.

jordan: closing the loop with customer now. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

maya: nice triage, great cross-team work.

jordan: marking resolved from support side but leaving thread open for ops follow-ups.
